name: Prokudin-Gorsky
findings: Uses alice blue 6.7x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1173 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dark hyssop violet turns up as a small accent in 40% of the paintings that hold it, 9.0x the archive's rate (from 1173 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, mossy green turns up as the shadow in 75% of the paintings that hold it, 9.3x the archive's rate (from 1173 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 1173 paintings here).
Rarely uses dark olive brown, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 1173 paintings here).
Pairs dark purple with deep rose red more than chance would predict (3 of 1173 paintings here).
Pairs dark purple with english red more than chance would predict (3 of 1173 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (alice blue, platinum, pale aqua) covers 65% of his paintings here.
